minutes.headline: Finance Committee voted 5-0 to transfer $5,000 from the reserve fund to cover the gap in the Mart transportation program.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the interim town manager on weights and measures inspection costs, which was deferred two weeks. It approved a reserve transfer to bridge the Mart transportation grant gap, then discussed capital funding, the budget calendar, the fall town meeting articles, a department budget presentation template, and a split tax rate comparison with Maynard.

votes.motion: Authorize transfer of $5,000 from the reserve account to the Council on Aging to cover the gap in the Mart transportation program for October and November.

votes.outcome: passed by roll call (all four members and chair voting aye)

budget_items.what_was_said: The inspector's salary was slotted at a small stipend; the inspector resigned and the town will contract with the state, costing considerably more.
The interim town manager expects a request in the FY26 budget and asked to defer for two weeks.
A member questioned the jump in cost given the same number of scanners.
The grant expires at month end and the town manager will request funds at fall town meeting to continue the program.
A gap between September 30 and about November 30 was estimated.
The COA director offered some formula grant money to offset the gap.
Estimates were discussed for the cost to continue the program through the end of the fiscal year and for FY26 if the town subsidizes it.
Committee moved a reserve transfer to cover the gap, with the COA covering any overage.
Only a small amount in the operating budget can go to new borrowing; other debt is under debt exclusions.
Remaining funds for roof, masonry and the Ritter building were described, and an account is running in the red.
A member noted the annual town meeting reapproves unspent capital funds without detail.

budget_items.topic: Free cash used to balance budget
budget_items.what_was_said: The interim town manager said free cash used this year creates a structural deficit going into the coming year.
The state sent additional Chapter 70 funds that the schools requested as a supplemental appropriation on the fall warrant.
Parks revolving fund balance has built up beyond the amount that should be swept to the general fund.
The bond would be fit into existing debt capacity, with debt smoothing discussed.
A line in the general government budget for grant writing was discussed, with hope it would bring in multiples of its cost.
Local receipts have been estimated conservatively, with actuals well over estimates.
A split tax rate would shift a levy amount from residents to commercial/industrial.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee voted 5-0 by roll call to move money from the reserve fund to the Council on Aging to cover a gap in the Mart transportation program.
The Mart transportation grant expires at month end, leaving an estimated gap of about two months before fall town meeting funds could continue the program.
A weights and measures funding item was deferred about two weeks after the inspector resigned and the town moved toward contracting with the state.
The interim town manager said free cash used to balance this year's budget creates a structural deficit going into the coming year.
The interim town manager is to add drop-dead dates to the budget calendar and send it within a day or two.

why_it_matters: The reserve transfer keeps a ride program running for residents who depend on it through the gap, and the grant's end means the town may be asked to fund it at fall town meeting.
Using free cash to balance one year's budget leaves a structural deficit going into the next, which bears on the FY26 budget and on future tax bills.
watch_next: The weights and measures funding item returns in about two weeks.
The revised budget calendar with drop-dead dates is due from the interim town manager within a day or two.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the one non-procedural vote, the $5,000 reserve fund transfer to the Council on Aging for Mart transportation, and on the main attendees, the free cash figure and the weights and measures deferral. They differ on the attendee list, where ours seats a sixth member (Bernard/Berard) beside the official's five present, and on the follow-up actions after the budget presentation template, which each describe differently. Many figures and several decisions appear in only one record.
